seal.statement: A successful harness image build (test/distributed/harness/docker-provider.js buildImage, the one build step every lab scenario and cone run uses per docker host for distributed-db:test) retires the image its tag named before the build: it records that id before building, and after the build removes it only when it is now untagged and no container, running or stopped, uses it, never forced. It touches nothing else - no prune, no other dangling image, never a tagged image (pinned product images, redis/node/distroless/pd/postgres bases) - and records the outcome as a typed operation event (recorded, removed, kept-in-use, kept-tagged, kept-remove-failed, kept-unverified, none). A step it cannot verify keeps the image, and retirement never fails the build.

text: New test/distributed/harness/docker-image-retirement.js (imageIdOf, retirePreviousImage, RETIREMENT outcomes). test/distributed/harness/docker-provider.js buildImage records the id its tag names before the build as an image.retire-previous 'recorded' event and, after a completed build, removes that image only when it is now untagged and no container (all: true) uses it, never forced, emitting the outcome (removed, kept-in-use, kept-tagged, kept-remove-failed, kept-unverified, none) with previousId, currentId and detail; it never throws and never touches another image. R17 records from the verification of 1c3c09dae. F6 (owner test/distributed/harness/docker-provider.js, safe): two runs building the same tag on one host at once can each record the same previous id; the first retires it, the second answers none (already gone) or kept for its own reason, and the image the first run's build produced can be left untagged when the second build moves the tag past it - one leftover per overlap, never a removal of something in use.
